question: GQ-007
subject: the long-s limit I said was permanent, fixed without touching the text
what_i_had_written: "Deliberately not fixed: normalising f->s would corrupt fuel, fund, fast" — a reason I stated without testing it

i_tested_it.verdict: the caveat was RIGHT — blind substitution would corrupt at scale. Stating it untested was still wrong.

the_rule_that_works: convert a word only when the f-form is NOT in /usr/share/dict/words and some s-substitution IS. Multi-f words need a subset search: firft->first (second f only), himfelf->himself, fatisfaction->satisfaction. The dictionary is the authority, not my judgement about which words look archaic.
built: scripts/add-longs-variants.mjs — a SEPARATE passage_modern FTS table; the original text is untouched

no_corruption.note: every genuine f-word is EXACTLY intact

three_bugs_of_my_own_on_the_way.cause: 2,000 full passage bodies exceeded the argv limit
passage bodies contain embedded newlines; splitting sqlite output on \n shreds one row into fragments — same defect that broke 40 titles into 154 pieces earlier today
three_bugs_of_my_own_on_the_way.fix: json_group_array, so sqlite escapes its own output

three_bugs_of_my_own_on_the_way.cause: I compared unscoped FTS matches: passage_ext_search covers heading+body, passage_modern covers body only. The row I "lost" had LETTERS FROM THE CONTINENT as its HEADING.
